newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae group pleased with second meeting.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae group pleased with second meeting.

text.p: A dissident shareholders group said Monday it was pleased that Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) shareholders have backed its call for a second special meeting.
"We're hopeful that they schedule the two meetings together," said Albert Lord of the Committee to Restore Value.

Lord said while the original meeting called by Sallie Mae management will allow shareholders to approve or reject a management reorganization plan, the second meeting, which his group had been seeking, will allow shareholders to vote on separate plans of reorganization and a separate slate of directors.

Lord said his group wants a business plan which is "more aggressive" than the company's plan. He said the management plan would confine Sallie Mae to the secondary market for student loans, while the Committee's plan would get Sallie Mae into the origination of student loans as a primary lender.
Asked to comment on the two plans, Sallie Mae spokeswoman Gisela Vallandigham said, "the biggest difference is that we haven't seen his plan."

She said the management believes it has a prudent business plan. "Our shareholders understand it and approved of it in the marketplace," she said. She added that the Sallie Mae stock price has tripled over the last two and one-half years and "we think that is testimony to the value of the plan we have had and will continue to have going forward."
Sallie Mae's announcement Monday said it understood that shareholders representing more than one-third of the outstanding shares have returned proxies calling for the second shareholders meeting.

The meeting originally called by Salie Mae is scheduled for May 15. In response to a question, a Sallie Mae spokesman said the time of the second meeting would be determined and announced "fairly shortly."
